transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-29 10:00am PT | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Karen Li (Acme CTO), Michael Brooks (Acme SRE), Priya Rao (Acme Security), Ethan Park (Acme Platform)

Summary: Quick sync focused on network connectivity issues that blocked last week's bench run, plus planning for the runtime upgrade and canary. We reviewed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Sophie Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll run quick agenda — network update, bench results, runtime upgrade and then next steps. can everyone hear ok?
[00:12] Karen Li: yes, can hear. thanks Sophie.
[01:05] Daniel Kim: ok to jump in on the network side — so we rechecked the config. the primary blocker was that the outbound rules from Acme's private subnet were dropping the tcp 443 to the control plane IPs; looks like a NAT gateway policy that wasn't forwarding. we have a note in the doc: redwood-private-networking.pdf (link: https://redwood.share/network-diagram).
[02:30] Michael Brooks: yeah i saw errors in the logs - we were getting connection resets at the TLS handshake step, intermittent. one oddity — the control plane was resolving to two IPs, one we whitelisted and one we didn't; split-horizon DNS within our VPC caused that.
[03:05] Aisha Patel: that split-horizon thing will bite the boot — we can provide a list of exact IPs and a CIDR range to whitelist. also we recommended using route table entries pointing to our private endpoint rather than public egress to avoid transient hairpinning.
[04:10] Priya Rao: quick sec — from security perspective we need to ensure that outbound traffic is restricted to those IPs and we get audit logs for all control-plane API calls. is that available?
[04:28] Daniel Kim: yes, audit logs are available — we can stream to your SIEM via our customer-managed syslog endpoint. there is an example config in the security appendix.
[05:30] Ethan Park: mic question — does Redwood require any BGP or peering setup? we prefer not to do direct peering.
[05:45] Sophie Martinez: no BGP needed. We support VPN and private endpoints inside your VPC, no BGP required for the pilot. if you wanted dedicated cross-connect later we can discuss.
[06:50] Daniel Kim: on routing: recommended approach is one route table with entries to the private endpoint's ENI; avoid NAT for control plane traffic. for inference nodes we'll use a separate subnet with no public egress, and the nodes will talk back to the management plane over the private link.
[08:10] Michael Brooks: ok, i'll produce the exact route table snippet. last week our bench run failed at step 2 (TLS) and we also saw the KV cache warm didn't persist across restarts — is that expected?
[08:45] Aisha Patel: hmm the KV cache persistence issue — we saw in the logs that the runtime version used had an earlier cache eviction policy. the upgrade to v1.8.2 addressed that, we should see much better cache affinity and lower repeated token regen. but the upgrade process requires a rolling restart across nodes to preserve serving capacity.
[09:30] Karen Li: rolling restart worries me a bit — we can't have downtime. what's the fallback?
[09:45] Daniel Kim: we do canary: spin up a small subset (10%) on the new runtime, route a fraction of traffic, validate latency and error rates, then increase. if canary fails we auto-rollback to pinned version. you can also pin model version/config to avoid model-variant mismatch.
[11:00] Sophie Martinez: quick note — we'll share the canary runbook and automated rollback policy after the call.
[11:35] Michael Brooks: on latency — our last bench showed a 12% increase at p95 on long-context chats compared to baseline; is that tied to runtime or to our network?
[12:00] Aisha Patel: initial hypothesis is a combination: the older runtime had inefficient attention kernel for long contexts; the v1.8.2 includes a new attention kernel which improves long-context performance but we need to validate under your sequence length distribution. also if requests are hairpinned through public NAT you'll see additional 10-40ms depending on path.
[13:20] Priya Rao: about logging — we need to keep request-level logs for 90 days for audit. does Redwood store any customer content? how is it encrypted?
[13:40] Daniel Kim: for Private deployments data-in-flight is TLS, and data-at-rest uses customer KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS/HSM). by default we don't retain raw customer payloads beyond ephemeral logs unless requested. we'll send the SOC2/ISO artifact set.
[15:00] Karen Li: perfect, please send SOC2 artifact list.
[15:10] Sophie Martinez: noted. we'll attach the security pack after the call.
[16:00] Ethan Park: on upgrades — what's the expected performance delta after v1.8.2? any numbers?
[16:20] Aisha Patel: internal perf tests show about 8-15% p95 reduction for long-chat workloads when using the new attention kernel plus cache persistence. small overhead on cold start for the first token while kernels warm up, but overall throughput improves due to fewer cache misses.
[17:50] Michael Brooks: ok we'll need to schedule a bench run that mimics our production sequences — mostly 2-4k tokens with some spikes to 12k. can you support that?
[18:10] Daniel Kim: yes, we can configure the bench harness to replay your trace files. please share a sanitized trace or sequence distribution and we'll run against the pilot cluster.
[19:00] Karen Li: timeline — we want a green bench by next week otherwise we'll push the pilot back.
[19:12] Sophie Martinez: understood. we'll prioritise network diagram and manifest updates so you can whitelist and then we'll run the bench.
[20:00] Michael Brooks: also one small gotcha — our infra team prefers IP allowlists over FQDN due to internal policy; can you provide static IP ranges?
[20:20] Daniel Kim: we can provide an explicit set of IPs/CIDR for the control plane; for data plane nodes the IPs are inside your VPC once provisioned so no external ranges needed.
[21:35] Priya Rao: on encryption KMS — we need proof that keys are customer-managed and that rotation doesn't break cache encryption.
[21:50] Aisha Patel: yes keys are customer-managed via AWS KMS; rotation is supported but we recommend a maintenance window for rotation to re-encrypt state. we'll include the rotation playbook.
[23:00] Karen Li: any risks we should be aware of before canary?
[23:10] Daniel Kim: main risk is an edge case with very long kv-key sets causing a temporary spike in memory while caches rebuild — mitigated by staged ramp and pinned fallback. also we monitor OOM and have auto-shed to keep latency SLOs.
[24:45] Sophie Martinez: ok let me recap next actions then we'll do Q&A — Redwood: share updated network diagram + IPs + canary runbook + security pack. Acme: share firewall rules, sanitized trace, confirm SOC2 artifacts required, schedule bench.
[25:10] Karen Li: yes that's right. one more question — pricing for Dedicated pilot if we need extra burst capacity during bench?
[25:25] Sophie Martinez: i'll send a pricing addendum — pilot includes a small burst allowance; anything beyond we'll quote and prorate.
[26:30] Michael Brooks: scheduling — confirm available window 10/05 for bench?
[26:45] Daniel Kim: 10/05 works from our side, we can do 9-12 PT slot.
[27:10] Ethan Park: we'll aim to have firewall rules applied by 10/03 so that bench can run with minimal friction.
[28:00] Priya Rao: one more on logs retention — if we stream to our SIEM do you have best-practice parsers we can drop in?
[28:15] Aisha Patel: yes we'll send a grok/parser example and the syslog schema.
[29:40] Karen Li: thanks all — anything else?
[29:50] Sophie Martinez: nope that's it, thanks everyone.

End recap & action items repeated: see action_items. Links shared during call: https://redwood.share/network-diagram (network), https://redwood.share/sec-pack (security/SOC2), https://redwood.share/canary-runbook (runbook).

Transcript notes: automated transcription had a few name mislabels (e.g., Michael/Mike) and some fillers. There were minor pauses and crosstalk between Michael and Daniel during the routing discussion.
